{"notes": "Visit 2 (ended 2:30). Board: a long chain is connected to the start. It runs along the belly and reaches the tail area (x~24-28), ending in a curl, and there is a tight, crowded cluster near x~24.5-25 that I want to check for a bad join. The back line is only partly built (pale, out to x~11) and is not connected to the start, so it would not fall as it stands. I can't tell who placed which dominoes, so I'm not crediting or blaming anyone for specific pieces.

Hana: Calm, clear coordination. Thanked Omar, said her lower fork will follow once the belly line arrives, and proposed a dry run of the tail join once the top and belly lines are across. Good process and leadership instincts. Her tail-first thinking is sound but I haven't seen her own work, so execution is still open. Check that the dry run actually happens.

Omar: Now speaking up and owning the upper tail fork, stroke 3, which is a clear step up from visit 1. The back line isn't across yet, so check his fork will connect to it, and that he's not building ahead of an unconnected line.

Sofia: Said nothing this visit. The belly line she was meant to trace is well advanced, but I can't confirm she laid it. Ask her next visit.

Jack: Silent this visit. The sketch evidently got done, since building is underway and fast. Check whether he is placing dominoes or only coordinating.

Team risks: the back line is disconnected and short, the tail cluster may be fragile, and 7.5 minutes remain. Next visit, check whether the back line gets joined to the start and who is fixing it."}
